name: Details
statusNote: Details is a styled wrapper on the HTML details element and is stable; it has almost no styling of its own. Its companion hook useDetails (controlled open state and close-on-outside-click) is what ActionMenu-era dropdowns were built on.
summary: A disclosure: a summary that toggles the visibility of the content after it. Use it for show-more sections and simple native-feeling dropdowns; use anchored-overlay for menus that must float, position and trap focus.

inputs.name: summary
inputs.description: The always-visible toggle (Details.Summary). It may render as another component, such as a Button, which then acts as the summary.

inputs.name: open
inputs.description: Whether the content is shown. Uncontrolled by default; useDetails makes it controlled.

inputs.name: closeOnOutsideClick
inputs.description: useDetails: close when a click lands outside this details element while open.

inputs.name: onToggle
inputs.description: Called after the open state changes.

inputs.name: onClickOutside
inputs.description: useDetails: called on an outside click before closing; it can cancel the close.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: The details element; no box styling of its own.

anatomy.name: Summary
anatomy.description: The first child, the toggle. The browser's disclosure triangle is removed, so the summary shows only what the caller puts in it (usually a button with a chevron or caret octicon).

anatomy.name: Content
anatomy.description: Everything after the summary; not laid out at all while closed.

layout.text: Details draws nothing itself: no padding, border, background or marker. The summary's list marker and the WebKit disclosure marker are hidden.
Content follows the summary in normal flow and is removed from layout while closed. Floating it as a dropdown is the caller's job (absolute positioning in the content).

states.text: Open: the content is laid out and drawn below the summary. There is no transition.
Closed: only the summary is drawn.

behaviour.text: Activating the summary (click, or Enter or Space while it has focus) toggles open and fires onToggle; the summary is a single tab stop.
With useDetails the open state lives in the caller: the toggle event is read back into state unless a handler cancelled it, and setOpen opens or closes programmatically.

With closeOnOutsideClick, while open, a click (on release, at the document) whose nearest enclosing details element is not this one calls onClickOutside and then closes unless the handler cancelled the event.
In development a Details without a summary child logs a warning; the browser would otherwise invent a default 'Details' summary.

accessibility.role: group (details) with a summary that acts as a disclosure button
semantics: The summary exposes expanded or collapsed state.
Escape does nothing; useDetails adds no Escape handling.

notes.text: All behaviour is the browser's details element: the summary's focusability, Enter and Space toggling, the expanded state exposed to assistive technology, removing closed content from layout and the accessibility tree, and the toggle event. A native build implements a disclosure: a focusable summary control with aria-expanded semantics that shows or hides the content region.

useDetails' outside test asks whether the click's nearest details ancestor is this one, so a click inside a nested details element within the open one counts as outside and closes the parent. Test containment instead.

useDetails listens for click (on release, bubbling) where Overlay listens for mousedown (on press, capture); a press that starts inside and releases outside behaves differently between the two, and a handler that stops propagation can keep a Details open.
Details.Summary rendered as another component passes it as='summary', so a Button summary still renders a summary element and keeps the toggle; a component that ignores as loses it.
Details reads no tokens; its look comes entirely from the summary and content the caller supplies.
